correctness.rationale: Transitive Klein-four stabilizers give exactly 5 orbit types; labelled exponential formula and conditional Poisson are exact. The saddle local CLT has suppressed nonzero peaks at pi and pi/2; deleting singleton orbits changes lattice span to 2 and gives parity factor 2. EF strategy at rank q preserves entire finite orbits; rank-q existential witnesses force q disjoint copies of all 5 types and sharp 11q total. Failure probability bounded by union Poisson lower tails divided by P(S=n). CHECK.py reproduces exact counts n<=7 and high precision coefficient ratio checks; finite checks are not the infinite proof. Fixed-rank limits only.

value.rationale: The natural question of what happens to the first-order theory when two random involutions are conditioned to commute has a definite qualitative answer distinct from unconstrained independence. The sharp rank-q minimal canonical model 11q, stretched-exponential error scale and parity-dependent 2 exp(-r_n) coefficient are motivated structural and probabilistic invariants, not arbitrary finite slices. Mathematical usefulness lies in exact effective FO decision and identification of a lattice obstruction in rare singleton-orbit loss.
